config: BitsAndBytesConfig(load_in_4bit=True, bnb_4bit_quant_type='nf4', bnb_4bit_compute_dtype=torch.bfloat16), bnb_4bit_use_double_quant False (its default), dtype=torch.bfloat16
how:
1. every tensor's name, dtype and shape from the local snapshot's safetensors headers (no weight data read);
  2. which weights bitsandbytes quantizes: every nn.Linear of the model built on the meta device from the snapshot's
     config, except the modules transformers keeps in full precision (transformers.quantizers.base.get_keys_to_not_convert,
     e.g. lm_head); everything else (embeddings, norms, biases, an unquantized head) stays bf16 (2 bytes per element);
  3. for every distinct shape of a quantized weight, the real tensor of decoder layer --check-layer is quantized on the
     GPU by bitsandbytes exactly as transformers does it (bnb.nn.Params4bit(..., quant_type="nf4",
     compress_statistics=False, quant_storage=torch.uint8).to("cuda")), and its bytes are counted: the packed 4-bit
     codes plus the quantization state's tensors (absmax per block, the 16-value code book); every weight of that
     shape is counted at those bytes.
Pure Python + torch + bitsandbytes; takes the GPU for seconds (one layer's weights).
